t: and he may put many to death in one day, and hang them and leave them hanging for many days. If necessary he may execute and hang even contrary to the ordinary law (that a court may execute only one person each day and may not leave a hanged person overnight — see Hilchot Sanhedrin 14:10, 15:7).

and his rulings in all these matters and similar ones are law. In these matters he is not bound by rules and statutes; rather he sets the rules and they are binding on the people (see also Hilchot Gezelah 5:11-12).

everything stated in the passage on the king, the king acquires. When the people asked Samuel for a king, he spelled out for them the rights of the king who would be chosen (the 'passage on the king', I Samuel 8:11-17), and the king is entitled to all the rights written there (these are the rights detailed here in halachot 1-7).

and they do his work for him, and he pays their wages. They are not like the warriors and choice young men who are permanently with the king and whose sustenance is his responsibility (above, 5:2); rather, the king pays them for their work (Lechem Mishneh).
or their value. If he wishes to take them permanently.
and concubines without ketubah and without kiddushin. A concubine is a woman set aside permanently for a particular man, without betrothal and marriage.
he acquires her merely by designating her. By designating her for himself as a concubine.
but a commoner is forbidden to have a concubine. Only a woman married to him by chuppah and kiddushin is permitted to a commoner (Hilchot Ishut 1:4).

only with a Hebrew maidservant, after yi'ud. A man who has purchased a Hebrew maidservant may designate her as a wife by telling her that she is his wife, and she is thereby betrothed to him even without kiddushin money (Hilchot Avadim 4:7).
and perfumers. Women who prepare ointments.
and he takes fields, olive groves and vineyards. The grain and fruit that grow there (Lechem Mishneh).
and he pays their value. Although he is permitted to take them without permission, he must pay their price.
a tithe of the seed crops, the trees and the animals. He regularly takes a tenth of them for himself without payment.

the King Messiah takes one thirteenth from all the lands that Israel conquers. When Israel conquers territory by a conquest of the many, it has the status of the Land of Israel, and the King Messiah takes one thirteenth of it while the rest is divided among the tribes of Israel (in contrast, territory that a king conquers privately for himself belongs to him alone, as below, 5:10 — Yad Pashut).
those executed by the king. Who were put to death by the king's command (see above, 3:8).
their property goes to the king. See also Hilchot Evel 1:9.
the treasures of kings. Of the conquered country.
and he takes half off the top. The king takes half of the plunder before it is divided among the others.
the soldiers. The fighters.
the war against the seven nations. The war to conquer the Land of Israel from the seven Canaanite nations who lived in it.
and the aid of Israel from an enemy that has attacked them. A defensive war against attackers.
by the decision of a court of seventy-one. With the agreement of the Great Sanhedrin (see also Hilchot Sanhedrin 5:1).
and he breaks through to make himself a road. He makes a road through private property in order to pass through it for the needs of the war.
to utterly destroy the seven nations. To kill the Canaanite inhabitants of the land (see below, 6:4).

and they have already perished. Most of them were wiped out by Israel in the time of King David, and only isolated individuals remained, who scattered and intermingled with other nations (Sefer HaMitzvot, positive commandment 187).
his evil deeds. That he came to fight Israel as they were on the way after leaving Egypt (Exodus 17:8, Deuteronomy 25:18).
and his ambush on the way. That he set an ambush for them.
in order to arouse hatred of him. So that the hatred toward him will not weaken.

remember it with the mouth, do not forget it in the heart. Regarding remembering Amalek's deed it says both 'remember' and 'do not forget'; this doubling teaches that it is not enough to remember his deed, but it must be mentioned aloud.
the lands that Israel conquers with a king, by the decision of a court. Or through a judge or prophet with the consent of most of Israel (see Hilchot Terumot 1:2).

this is a conquest of the many and it is like the Land of Israel. But a place that a family or a tribe conquered for itself is called a conquest of an individual and is not considered like the Land of Israel (ibid.).

provided they conquer it after the conquest of the whole Land of Israel mentioned in the Torah. Territory conquered by a conquest of the many is considered the Land of Israel only if the conquest took place after the conquest of the land of the seven Canaanite nations (see Numbers 34:1-12). Therefore the lands that King David conquered before the conquest of the Land was completed are not considered the Land of Israel for all purposes (see Hilchot Terumot 1:3).
from the Mediterranean Sea in the west. The Mediterranean Sea, which lies north of Egypt, called thus because it serves as the western border of the Land of Israel.
four hundred parsa. About 1,600 kilometers.
opposite the land of Cush. Which is south of Egypt.
and opposite the desert. West of Egypt.

in three places the Torah warned not to return to Egypt. Although these verses are written as narrative and not as a command, the Sages received by tradition that they are warnings (Sefer HaMitzvot, negative commandment 46).

and Alexandria is included in the prohibition. The four hundred parsa are measured in length and width from the sea at the shore of Alexandria, and this is the area of the land of Egypt where settling is forbidden (ibid.).
for trade and business. Commerce and conducting business.
and to conquer other lands. To pass through it for the purpose of conquering other lands.
and it is forbidden only to settle there. To live there permanently.
and one is not lashed for this negative commandment, since at the time of entering it is permitted. For he has not yet settled.
and if he thinks of living and settling there, there is no act in it. And one is lashed only for a negative commandment that involves an act (Hilchot Sanhedrin 18:1).
as it says, 'like the practice of the land of Egypt'. The Torah defines forbidden sexual relations and abominable practices as 'the practice of the land of Egypt'.
to study Torah. Even if he has the possibility of studying in the Land, but prefers to study with a sage who is outside the Land (Kesef Mishneh; see Hilchot Evel 3:14).
to save from the hands of the gentiles. Money, for example if he must litigate with them (Kesef Mishneh).
and he returns to the Land. Even when one leaves in a permitted way, the departure must be for a limited time, and he must return when he finishes.
but to dwell outside the Land. Permanently.
until a dinar's worth of wheat sold for two dinars. The price of grain became double its usual price.
when money was available. There was a way to earn money.
if produce was cheap and he could not find money or a way to earn. Even though there is no famine, he cannot find a way to support himself and earn a living.
and although it is permitted to leave etc.. A permanent departure at a time of famine or when there is no money.
Machlon and Chilyon etc.. The sons of Elimelech, who went down with him to live in Moab because of a famine in Bethlehem and died there (see Ruth 1:1-5).
they would kiss the borders of the Land of Israel. When they came from outside the Land and entered the boundary of the Land of Israel.

and let no one say, 'I am sick'; the people who dwell there are forgiven their iniquity. One who lives in the Land should not be distressed by his illnesses, since the Holy One, blessed be He, bears his iniquity and forgives him.

and one who is received by it during life is not like one received by it after death. The merit of one who arrives in the Land alive is greater than that of one who dies outside the Land and is buried in the Land.

for they have driven me out today from clinging to the inheritance of the Lord, saying, 'Go, serve other gods'. David said this about the persecution by Saul, which caused him to leave for outside the Land.

so it is forbidden to leave Babylonia for other lands. Except the Land of Israel, to which one may go from Babylonia (Arukh HaShulchan 74:18, Michtam LeDavid, Even HaAzel). Some explain that this prohibition includes even the Land of Israel, and it is forbidden to leave Babylonia for there (Kesef Mishneh).
optional war... obligatory war. For their definitions see above, 5:1.
the seven commandments that the descendants of Noah were commanded. The commandments by which gentiles are bound (explained below, chapter 8).
we do not listen to them. And we fight them.
despised and lowly, and they shall not raise their heads in Israel. They will be subject to Israel and inferior to them in status.
ready for the king's service with their persons and property. The king may use them and their money for his needs as he wishes.
the fortresses. Strongholds (in many manuscripts the reading is 'the strongholds', but the reading here is based on II Chronicles 11:11 — according to Rabbi Y. Shilat in Rambam Meduyak).
and the king may stipulate with them that he take half of their property. As a tax taken from their property.

as it says, 'and the women and the children'. In the preceding verse it says, 'and you shall strike every male with the edge of the sword.' Then it says, 'Only the women and the children... you shall plunder for yourself,' from which we learn that the women (adult and minor) and the male children are left alive.
the seven nations. The inhabitants of the land of Canaan.

so shall you do etc.. Leaving the women and children alive applies only to the distant cities, but in the cities of the nations in the land of Canaan, no soul is left alive if they have not made peace.
except the Hivites, inhabitants of Gibeon. The Gibeonites, who tricked Israel so that they would make a covenant with them (as explained in the next halachah).

for it was from the Lord to harden their hearts to come against Israel in battle, in order to destroy them utterly. The Lord strengthened their resolve not to make peace with Israel, and thereby it became permitted to kill them.
Joshua sent three letters. To the Canaanite inhabitants of the land.
why did the people of Gibeon use trickery. They disguised themselves as people from distant cities so that Israel would leave them alive (see Joshua 9:3-13).
that he sent to them along with the rest. Along with the other cities of Canaan.
and they imagined that peace would not be offered to them. They thought that since they had not at first accepted the call to peace, Israel would no longer accept them.

and why was the matter hard for the princes etc.. When the trick was discovered they wanted to kill them, and refrained because the princes of Israel had sworn to them and made a covenant with them (ibid. 9:18-19).
because they had made a covenant with them. Even when they make peace with Israel it is forbidden to make a covenant with them; rather they are to be made slaves and taxed.

and since they swore to them in error etc.. The oath they swore to the Gibeonites in error did not bind them, yet they refrained from killing them because it would be a desecration of God's name if they broke the covenant.
we do not offer them peace. Rather we fight them immediately.
for it says, 'and you shall call to it for peace'. Regarding wars against the cities of the other nations.
if they made peace on their own first, we accept them. If before Israel came to fight them they accepted upon themselves taxation, servitude and the seven Noahide commandments, they are not killed.
when besieging a city to capture it. Laying siege in preparation for conquest.
we do not surround it on four sides but only on three. They surround the city from three directions and leave one side from which whoever wants to escape the city may flee.
from the oral tradition. The tradition of the Sages in explaining the verses.
outside the city. The surroundings of the city that they wish to conquer.
and we do not cut off the water channel from them. We do not divert from them the water that flows to them.
because its value is high. The price of the tree once cut is higher than the price of its fruit, and it is not worth leaving it to keep bearing fruit.
and he does only a small thing that is not worth the trouble. The quantity of fruit that the tree yields does not justify the effort.
a kav. About 1.4 liters.
whoever breaks vessels and tears clothing... violates 'do not destroy'. See also Hilchot Evel 14:24.

violates 'do not destroy' and is lashed only with makkat mardut, by rabbinic law. There is a Torah prohibition against destroying anything, but the Torah-mandated lashes apply only to destroying trees (since the Torah explicitly mentions only trees — Minchat Chinuch, commandment 529; Arukh HaShulchan 75:15); for destroying other things one is liable to makkat mardut by rabbinic law.

we besiege gentile cities on Shabbat. If the siege began before Shabbat it is continued on Shabbat, but one may not initially begin a siege on Shabbat, rather at least three days before Shabbat (Hilchot Shabbat 30:13; see also ibid. 2:25).
until it falls. One must besiege the city and fight against it until the conquest is completed and the city is under control.
when they encamp. The soldiers going out to war.
they encamp anywhere. Even without the permission of the owner of the place where they encamp.
and one who is killed in war is buried where he falls. They may bury him where he fell, and the owner of the land cannot prevent his burial there.
acquires his place like a met mitzvah. Just as a met mitzvah, who lies on the road with no one to bury him, acquires the place where he is and is buried there (Hilchot Rotzeach 9:9).
and four things were exempted in the camp. The fighters were given leniencies in them.

they may eat demai. Produce of ignorant people from which the Sages required separating terumat ma'aser and ma'aser sheni (Hilchot Ma'aser 9:2); in the camp they permitted eating demai without needing to separate.
and they are exempt from washing their hands initially. They are exempt from washing hands before eating bread, but are obligated in the after-meal washing (Hilchot Berakhot 6:3).
and they bring all kinds of wood from anywhere. Without the owners' permission.
even if they find it detached and dry. Which the owners surely care about and is not ownerless.

from establishing eruvei chatzerot. The Sages ordained that one may not carry in a courtyard containing separate domains of different people, even if it is surrounded by partitions and is a private domain, unless all the residents of the courtyard share one food, placed in a place designated as common to all (Hilchot Eruvin 1:2).
so that it be a private domain, as explained in Hilchot Shabbat. 14:1.
and a camp is no fewer than ten. Soldiers.
so too they are exempt on their return. When returning from war. For if we do not make things easier for them on the way back too, they will refrain from going out in the future (Radbaz).
to relieve himself. For his needs.
to prepare a special path there for relieving oneself. A special place where they will relieve themselves.
and you shall have a place. A place will be yours.
a peg. A digging tool.
your ear. The war implement.
that the Ark is with them. That they took the Ark of the Covenant out with them to the camp.
obligatory war... optional war. Above, 5:1.
and they anoint him with the anointing oil. See also Hilchot Kelei HaMikdash 1:7.
on the border. Near the frontier.
before they arrange the battle lines. Before the soldiers are set in formation for battle.

he says to them, 'Who is the man who has planted a vineyard...' When he hears my words, he returns from the battle lines. The priest tells those who must return from the war to prepare to return when he speaks a second time, at the arranging of the battle lines (Kesef Mishneh).

at the battle lines he says, 'Do not fear and do not be alarmed etc.'. And he continues: 'Who is the man who built a house... planted a vineyard... betrothed a wife... let him go and return to his house' (as explained below, halachah 3).
when they arrange the battle lines. When the soldiers are set in formation for battle.
Hear, O Israel. Listen.
let your heart not be faint. Do not be afraid.
and do not be alarmed. Do not be hasty.
and do not tremble. Do not be broken.
up to here the anointed for war speaks. All at once.

and another priest after him announces to all the people in a loud voice. Before the anointed priest goes on to say 'Who is the man who has built a new house...', another priest repeats his words aloud.
and the officer announces to all the people in a loud voice. An officer in charge of the army's battle lines repeats the words of the anointed priest in a loud voice.
and another officer announces to all the people. In a loud voice.
they prepare the battle lines. They ready them for fighting.
and they appoint commanders at the head of the people. They appoint officers, because after some have returned from the battle lines, reorganization is needed (Sforno on Deuteronomy 20:9).
and iron-bars. Rods.
for the beginning of a fall is flight. Fleeing causes defeat in war.
in what case is it said that they send back etc.. Therefore the proclamation 'Who is the man...' was not made in an obligatory war (Raavad and Kesef Mishneh, above, halachah 1).
a bridegroom from his room and a bride from her chuppah. A bridegroom and bride within the seven days of the wedding feast.
a cattle shed. A barn.
a wood shed. Where wood is stored.
a storehouse. A warehouse.
the purchaser. The buyer.
he returns. From the war, when he built, bought or received one of these houses and has not yet begun to live in it.
a gatehouse. A structure next to the gate of the house.
a portico. The open area in front of the house.

and a balcony. A platform raised above the courtyard from which one ascends by steps to the upper floors. These structures are not suitable for dwelling, and therefore one does not return on account of them.
the same applies to one who plants a vineyard etc.. All of these return from the war if the fruit of their planting is still orlah and they have not yet begun to eat from it.
vineyard. Grapes.
even of the five kinds of food. Even if each tree is of a different kind.
one who layers. Bends a branch of a tree and buries it in the ground so that another tree grows from it.
one who grafts. Attaches a cutting or branch to the trunk of an already planted tree.

layering and grafting that are subject to orlah. The layering and grafting for which one returns are those done in such a way that the layered or grafted branch is considered a new planting, and the years of orlah must be counted anew (see Hilchot Ma'aser Sheni and Neta Revai 10:14).
the same applies to one who betroths a virgin etc.. All of these return from the war if they have not yet married the women they betrothed.
one who betroths. One who sanctifies a woman to himself in marriage.

a yevamah fell to him. If his brother died childless, he must perform yibbum (marry) or chalitzah with his wife. Until he actually marries her, he has the status of one who betrothed a woman but has not yet married her.
all of them return. For each of them is fit to marry the yevamah.

he betrothed a woman 'from now, after twelve months'. If when he betrothed her he stipulated with her that the betrothal take effect in twelve months, and she is then considered betrothed already from now.

and the time was completed during the war, he returns. For when the time is completed it is clear that she was already married before the war (but if he did not say 'from now' but 'you are betrothed to me after twelve months' and the time was completed during the war, he does not return, since at the start of the war she was not yet married — Radbaz, Kesef Mishneh).
and one who betroths a woman forbidden to him etc.. Even in cases of negative-commandment prohibitions in which kiddushin takes effect (like the examples brought here; see Hilchot Ishut 1:7).
and a chalutzah. A yevamah whom the yavam released by chalitzah and who is thereby permitted to any man; she is forbidden to a kohen like a divorcee.
a mamzeret. Born of forbidden incestuous relations.

and a netinah. The Gibeonites were from the nations of Canaan and converted by deceit; they were given to the service of the Temple, and the Sages decreed a prohibition against marrying them, as with mamzerim (see Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 12:22-23).
they return and supply water etc.. Although they do not fight, they do not return to their homes but are assigned rear-line tasks.
and we do not trouble them with anything in the world. Even supplying water and food.
and dedicated it. Began to live in it.
performed yibbum. Married his yevamah.
who redeemed his vineyard. Who ate the fruit of his vineyard in the fourth year, when the fruit is neta revai and to eat it must be redeemed with money (Hilchot Ma'aser Sheni and Neta Revai 9:1-2).

he shall be free for his house etc.. The verse speaks of one who takes a new wife, who in the first year of his marriage does not go out with the army and is not burdened with other needs of the army and the city (see next halachah); and it was learned by tradition that the same applies to one who dedicated a house or redeemed a vineyard.
for the city walls. A tax for guarding the city.
and it shall not pass over him. It shall not be imposed upon him.

to transgress on his account two negative commandments. The negative commandment is doubled to reinforce the prohibition (but these are not two separate negative commandments — see Sefer HaMitzvot, ninth principle, and negative commandment 'shin-alef').
for the needs of the city. Strengthening its security.
for the needs of the troop. Assisting the fighters.
and he paid him his wages in advance. He gave him the rent at the beginning of the rental period.
it is as if he dedicated it. From the moment he actually received the rent and benefited from the house, he has the status of one who dedicated the house.
he built a house, put his belongings in it and locked them in. And did not actually begin to live in it.

if he had to stop working to guard them, then etc.. If before putting them into the house he had to stop his work in order to guard the items he brought in, it turns out that even though he has not yet lived in the house, he has benefited from it.
who is the man who is fearful and fainthearted. Of whom the verse goes on to say, 'let him go and return to his house.'
who lacks the strength in his heart to stand in the ranks of war. Out of fear he is unable to take part in battles.
the hope of Israel and its savior in time of trouble. The Holy One, blessed be He, for whom Israel hopes and who saves them (based on Jeremiah 14:8).
for he wages war for the unity of the Name. For the war against the people of Israel is a war against the Lord.
and he shall put his life in his hand. He will give up his life (based on Judges 12:3).
for all the blood of Israel hangs on his neck. The loss is charged against him.
he prevailed. He overcame.
in the Prophets. The words of the prophets.

cursed be he who does the Lord's work deceitfully, and cursed be he who withholds his sword from blood. The verse deals with Israel's war with Moab, and says that those who do not fight properly and refrain from killing the enemy shall be cursed.
for the Lord will surely make my lord a sure house etc.. So Abigail said to David.
a sure house. Stable, established and secure.
in the bundle of life. The World to Come.

when they enter the border of the gentiles, conquer them and take captives from them, it is permitted for them to eat etc.. The permission applies during the fighting and while remaining in enemy territory (but before they leave the border it is forbidden for them to eat forbidden foods — Radbaz).
if he is hungry and found nothing to eat but these forbidden foods. When no permitted food is available to him (and not only in a life-threatening situation — Radbaz, Kesef Mishneh).
wine of libation. Wine that was poured as a libation to idols, which is ordinarily forbidden for drinking and any benefit (Hilchot Ma'achalot Asurot 11:1).
from the oral tradition. The tradition of the Sages in explaining the verses.

and houses full of all good things. This verse was said about the time of entering the Land, that during the war to conquer the Land they would be able to eat of the foods they found in the Canaanites' houses, and the Sages expounded that this applies even if forbidden foods are there.
pig's neck-meat. The meat of a pig's neck.
in her gentile state. While she is a gentile.
but he brings her into his house. In order to convert her and marry her (see below, halachot 5-7).
at the time of capture. And not afterward, at the end of the war (unless he marries her, as explained below, halachot 5-6).

for gentiles have no marriage. A gentile's wife is not considered a married woman with regard to Israelites, and therefore she too is permitted (but with regard to gentiles she is considered married — see Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 14:19, below 9:5).
that he not press her in war. That he not have relations with her on the battlefield.

a kohen is permitted to a beautiful captive in the first relation. A gentile woman is considered a zonah and is forbidden to kohanim (Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 18:1), and nevertheless, for the first relation the Torah permitted him to have relations with her.

for the Torah spoke only against the evil inclination. The entire permission to have relations with a beautiful captive is only because of the strength of the inclination in wartime (for even an Israelite is forbidden to have relations with a woman other than through kiddushin and marriage). For this reason it was also permitted to a kohen, even though she is ordinarily forbidden to him.
but he cannot marry her afterward, because she is a convert. And she is forbidden to a kohen (ibid. 3:3).
he immerses her immediately for the sake of conversion. So as to marry her afterward (as explained below, halachah 6).
she shall remain in his house thirty days. During which she mourns her parents from whom she has been separated (see Hilchot Evel 6:1).
and so she weeps for her religion. The Sages expounded the wording 'and she shall weep for her father and her mother' as referring also to her idolatry (see Sifrei, Ki Teitzei 213).
so that he will loathe her. Find her repulsive.
and he persuades her. Convinces and urges her.
that she accept. Be persuaded to convert.
and she must wait three months. Before he marries her, so that if she is found pregnant there will be no doubt about the lineage of the child (see Hilchot Gerushin 11:21).
if he kept her after she had relations as a maidservant. He held on to her and kept her with him to be his maidservant.
you shall not treat her tyrannically. Use her.
we persuade her for a full twelve months. For a similar law regarding a slave, see Hilchot Avadim 8:12.
the seven commandments that the descendants of Noah were commanded. Below, chapter 9.
resident aliens. Gentiles who accepted upon themselves not to worship idols and to keep the commandments that the descendants of Noah were commanded (see below, halachah 10).
that he is forbidden to marry a woman who has not converted. Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 12:1.

if she became pregnant from the first relation, the child is a convert etc.. One born of an Israelite and a gentile woman is considered a gentile and is not considered the Israelite's son (Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 12:9). However, the court converts him on their own authority (see ibid. 13:7, below 10:3).
and Tamar became pregnant from the first relation of a beautiful captive. Tamar, Absalom's sister, was David's daughter from a beautiful captive he took, and she is not considered his daughter.
and she was permitted to marry Amnon. Who was David's son from another wife.
and so a city that made peace etc.. When peace was offered to it before the war (see also above, 6:4).

and one who accepts them is called a ger toshav everywhere. He is called this because it is permitted to settle him in the Land of Israel (Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 14:7; see also Hilchot Avodah Zarah 10:6).
and he must accept upon himself. To abandon idolatry and keep the Noahide commandments.
before three associates. Who serve as a court.
and anyone who accepts circumcision upon himself. A ger toshav who accepted upon himself to be circumcised, though not obligated.

he is like one of the nations' sectarians. Since he accepted circumcision and did not circumcise, we assume that he did so out of denial, and we do not treat him as a ger toshav whom it is a mitzvah to keep alive, but as a gentile (see Babylonian Talmud Avodah Zarah 65a).
and anyone who does not accept shall be put to death. This refers to one who openly and publicly espouses idolatry (Yad Pashut).
conviction of the mind. That he understood on his own that this is right and proper to do.
blessing the Name. The prohibition of cursing God's name.
courts of law. To appoint judges (below, halachah 14).
for all of them are a tradition in our hands from Moses our teacher. These commandments that the descendants of Noah were commanded were transmitted by tradition from Moses our teacher.
and the mind inclines toward them. A person understands with his intellect that he must observe them.

from the whole of the words of the Torah it appears that they were commanded about these. This can also be inferred from the Torah's stories, which describe people being punished for these acts (Yad Pashut).
but flesh with its life, its blood, you shall not eat. From this we learn that it is forbidden to eat the flesh while the animal is still alive ('with its life, its blood').
and he prayed in the morning, and Isaac separated a tithe etc.. They did these commandments on their own even though they had not been commanded to (Kesef Mishneh).
another prayer toward the end of the day. The Minchah prayer, which is toward the end of the day.

the sciatic nerve. The nerve on the hip joint of an animal's leg, which is forbidden to eat (Hilchot Ma'achalot Asurot 8:1). Already from the time of our forefather Jacob they observed this prohibition (see Genesis 32:33).
Amram. Moses' father.
a descendant of Noah who worshiped idols is liable. To death by the sword (below, halachah 14).
that he worship in its usual way. In the manner in which that idol is worshiped.
and any idolatry for which an Israelite court puts to death. If an Israelite worshiped it (see Hilchot Avodah Zarah 3:2-3).
for which an Israelite court does not put to death. For example, if he worshiped it in a way other than its usual way (see ibid. halachah 6).
to set up a pillar. A structure where people gather for worship (ibid. 6:6).
to plant an asherah. To plant a tree for idolatry.

to make figures and the like for ornament. Statues and reliefs of people and celestial bodies. It was forbidden to make them so that people would not err and think they are for idolatry (ibid. 3:10-11).
who blessed. Who cursed.

whether he blessed with the unique Name. One of the names of God that may not be erased (see Hilchot Keriat Shema 3:5; for their details see Hilchot Yesodei HaTorah 6:2). For example, if he said that the unique Name should strike the Name.

or blessed with a substitute name. One of the epithets with which God is praised, such as 'Gracious', 'Merciful' and the like (ibid. 6:5). For example, if he said that the epithet should strike the Name.
he is liable. To death by the sword.
which is not so for Israelites. Who are liable only when they curse the Name using one of the names that may not be erased (Hilchot Avodah Zarah 2:7).
even a fetus in its mother's womb is killed for. But an Israelite who kills a fetus is not put to death, since it is not considered fully alive (see Hilchot Rotzeach 1:9).

and so too if he killed a terefah. A person with a severe defect that will cause death within a short time and for which there is no cure, who is considered dead to some extent; therefore an Israelite who kills him is not put to death by a court (ibid. 2:8).

who bound him and placed him before a lion. And the lion killed him. An Israelite who did this is considered a shedder of blood and is liable to death at the hands of Heaven, but is not liable to death by a court since he caused the death indirectly (ibid. 2:2).
or left him in hunger until he died. An Israelite who did this is a murderer but is not put to death by a court (ibid. 3:10).

if he killed a pursuer when he could have saved the victim by [injuring] one of his limbs etc.. If someone is pursuing another to kill him, it is permitted to kill the pursuer in order to save the victim. But if the victim can be saved by injuring one of the pursuer's limbs, it is forbidden to kill the pursuer (ibid. 1:6-7). An Israelite who could have saved the victim by [injuring] one of the pursuer's limbs and did not bother to do so but killed him is a shedder of blood and liable to death, but the court does not put him to death (ibid. halachah 13); a descendant of Noah, however, is put to death for this.
six forbidden sexual relations are forbidden to the descendants of Noah etc.. See also Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 14:10.
and a male. Homosexual intercourse.
and it says, 'she is my sister, the daughter of my father but not the daughter of my mother' etc.. From which it follows that his maternal sister is forbidden but not his paternal sister.
one who was seduced by his father, or raped by his father, is his mother. He is forbidden to his mother even if she was not his father's wife.
and he is liable for a male, whether a minor or an adult. But an Israelite is not liable to death for relations with a minor (Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 1:14).
and he alone is put to death, and the animal is not killed. But an animal that was mated with by an Israelite is killed (ibid. halachah 16).
betrothed. That he designated her to himself as a wife.
who entered the chuppah. Was married.
and she is married to a husband. Said to Abimelech as a rebuke for taking Sarah.
but a gentile who had relations with an Israelite woman. Who is a married woman. But one who has relations with an unmarried woman is not put to death (Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 12:9).
not in the usual way. From behind; and he is liable to death just as for Israelites there is liability to death also for relations not in the usual way (ibid. 1:10).

and if she was a betrothed girl, he is stoned as in the laws of Israel. As an Israelite who had relations with a betrothed girl (ibid. 1:6). He is not judged by the sword, the death of the descendants of Noah, since for descendants of Noah such relations do not carry a death penalty.

by strangulation, as in the laws of Israel. As an Israelite who had relations with a married woman (ibid.), since among descendants of Noah there is no prohibition in the case of one who entered the chuppah and was not yet had relations with.

if he had relations with the wife of an Israelite after she had been had relations with etc.. Since even for descendants of Noah such relations are forbidden, he is put to death by the death of the descendants of Noah.
who designated a maidservant for his slave. That she be permanently with this slave; although the slave and maidservant did not marry each other of their own will, she is considered his wife.
he is put to death for her. Another descendant of Noah who had relations with her.
so that the matter will spread. The report will spread.
the maidservant of such-and-such slave. The girl of so-and-so.
and let her uncover her head in the marketplace. Remove the head covering from her head in public, in the manner of an unmarried woman.

for she has no written divorce, and the matter does not depend on him alone. Unlike Israelite marriages, in which a divorce must be by a written get, and the husband alone is the one who divorces (Hilchot Gerushin 1:1-2).
the robber. By force and openly.
or the thief. In secret.
who withholds a hired worker's wages. Delays payment of wages.

even a worker who ate not at the time of work. But at the time of work, a worker who works with the produce of the ground is permitted to eat (Hilchot Sekhirut 12:1; this law applies also with a gentile — see Sha'ar HaMishpat, Choshen Mishpat 337, subsection 1; Minchat Chinuch, commandment 576).
he is liable for everything. Death.
which is not so for Israelites. Who are not liable for all these as theft (Kesef Mishneh).
and so he is liable for less than a perutah's worth. Unlike an Israelite, who does not violate theft for less than a perutah's worth (Hilchot Gezelah 1:1).
both of them are put to death for it. For the second one stole from the first, and therefore he too is put to death.
a limb from a living animal... flesh from a living animal. A limb or piece of flesh cut from an animal while it was alive (for their definitions see Hilchot Ma'achalot Asurot 5:2).

in any amount, for the measures were given only to Israelites. He is liable for eating them in any size, even less than an olive's bulk. But Israelites are liable for eating a limb from a living animal only when they eat the measure of an olive's bulk (ibid. halachah 3).
blood from a living animal. Blood that came out of the animal while it was alive.

but as for a bird, it seems to me that a descendant of Noah is not put to death for a limb from a living bird. Although for Israelites the prohibition of a limb from a living animal applies also to birds (Hilchot Ma'achalot Asurot 5:1).
one who slaughters the animal. Who slaughtered the animal properly and made it fit for an Israelite to eat.

even if he slaughtered both signs. Even if he cut both signs of slaughter (the windpipe and the gullet) completely, which is the optimal slaughter (whereas by law even if he cut most of each sign of slaughter it is valid — Hilchot Shechitah 1:9).
as long as it is convulsing. As long as it moves its limbs after slaughter, so it has not yet died entirely.
a limb or flesh that separates from it is forbidden to the descendants of Noah as a limb from a living animal. Although for Israelites these are not considered a limb from a living animal.

for descendants of Noah, whether an animal or a wild beast, whether pure or impure, are liable for it. Whereas Israelites are not liable for a limb from a living animal for one that separates from an impure animal (Hilchot Ma'achalot Asurot 5:1).
in every district. In every region.
by the sword. With a blade.
all the lords of Shechem. The inhabitants of the city.
Shechem robbed. Dinah (see Genesis chapter 34).

by one witness and one judge etc.. Unlike an Israelite, who is judged on the testimony of two witnesses and by three judges, and is punished only if warned before the act, and whose relatives are disqualified from testifying for him.
but not on the testimony of a woman. A woman is disqualified from testifying and judging in their courts, as in Israelite courts.
exempt from anything. He is not punished at all.

except for an unintentional murderer, for if the blood avenger kills him, he is not put to death for it etc.. When a person kills unintentionally, a relative of the one killed (the 'blood avenger') may kill the murderer. However, if the murderer flees to a city of refuge, the blood avenger is forbidden to kill him, and if he does so he is liable to death. Since the descendant of Noah has no law of cities of refuge (the cities of refuge do not take him in, and even inside them the blood avenger may kill him), he has no protection from the blood avenger, and if the avenger kills him, the avenger is not put to death (see Hilchot Rotzeach 5:4).
that a coercer coerced him. Forced him.

even if he was coerced to worship idols, he worships, since they are not commanded regarding sanctification of the Name. But an Israelite is commanded to sanctify the Name, and is forbidden to worship idols even if he will be killed by the coercer (Hilchot Yesodei HaTorah 5:2).
neither a minor, nor a deaf-mute, nor a mentally incompetent person, since they are not subject to mitzvot. For they lack understanding.
and he circumcised and immersed. By these acts the gentile completes his conversion process (Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 13:4-5).
and to be only a ger toshav, as he was before. And to keep only the seven Noahide commandments (above, 8:10).
or be put to death. If he insists on considering himself a gentile, he is considered an apostate and is treated as an apikores (Even HaAzel).

and if he was a minor when the court immersed him etc.. In certain cases (such as above, 8:8) a court immerses a minor on its own authority, since it is a privilege to be an Israelite (see Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 13:7); but if he protests when he grows up, he returns to being a ger toshav.
at that time. Immediately upon becoming an adult.
if she comes to her ketubah money, a minor girl whom the court immersed. If she is entitled to receive her ketubah money, for example if her husband died or divorced her.
the fine of a rapist or seducer. If she was raped or seduced, and the rapist or seducer must pay her (see Hilchot Na'arah Betulah 1:1).
it all shall be under the court's control etc.. The money will be held for her by the court, and only when it is finally established that she is indeed Jewish will she receive it.
lest she take it, grow up and protest. And return to the status of a ger toshav.

who blessed the Name or worshiped idols... and converted is exempt. Since after his conversion his death penalty has changed to a more severe one (for previously he was liable for these acts to the sword and now he is liable for them to stoning), he cannot be held liable to this death and is exempt (see Babylonian Talmud Sanhedrin 71b).

who had relations with his neighbor's wife or killed his neighbor and converted is exempt. Since if he were to commit this act now he would not be liable to death, he is not put to death for what he did earlier (Rashi, ibid.).

and we put him to death for the son of an Israelite. He is put to death by the sword for an Israelite's son whom he killed while he was a gentile, for this death is the same for Israelites and descendants of Noah, and even now if he killed an Israelite he would be liable to death by the sword.

and we strangle him for the wife of an Israelite whom he had relations with, for his law has changed. Although a descendant of Noah who had relations with a married woman is put to death by the sword, after he converted and became an Israelite he is put to death by strangulation, like an Israelite who had relations with a married woman. In this case he is not exempt from punishment, since death by the sword is more severe than death by strangulation (see Hilchot Sanhedrin 14:4), and therefore the strangulation penalty he is now liable for is included in the sword penalty he incurred while a gentile (Babylonian Talmud, ibid.).
we have already explained. Above, 9:7.

but if he had relations with the wife of an Israelite, a betrothed girl, he is stoned. Therefore even if he converted after having had relations with her, he is put to death by stoning, and there is no stricter ruling in his case.
and if he had relations with her after she entered the chuppah and before she had relations, he is strangled. And so he is punished even if he converted (see Merkevet HaMishneh and Yad Pashut).
from the oral tradition. According to the tradition of the Sages.
by mating animals. Mating animals of these different kinds with each other (see Hilchot Kilayim 9:2).
and by grafting a tree. Inserting a detached branch of one kind of tree into a tree of another kind so that it fuses with it (see ibid. 1:6).
only. The descendants of Noah were not forbidden other kinds of diverse kinds, such as diverse seeds and diverse garments.
even if he wounded him. If he made a wound from which blood came out, even without striking him a hard blow.
although he is liable to death, he is not put to death. By a court (see also Hilchot Chovel 5:3).

Abraham and his descendants only etc.. Jacob and his descendants are considered the continuers of Abraham's seed, but not Ishmael and Esau (see also Hilchot Nedarim 9:21 and see Commentary on the Mishnah, Nedarim 3:11).

for through Isaac shall your seed be called. God tells Abraham not to be concerned about sending Ishmael out of his house, since the seed that will be called by his name is specifically through Isaac and not Ishmael.
he may engage only in the seven commandments that are theirs alone. He is permitted to study only the laws of his own commandments.
and so a gentile who rested. On Shabbat.
and needless to say if he made a festival for himself. If he invented a holiday that does not exist at all among Israelites.
he shall stand by his own Torah. The seven Noahide commandments.
a descendant of Noah. One who keeps the Noahide commandments.
who wished to perform a commandment from the other commandments of the Torah. Other than Torah study and Shabbat rest.
we do not prevent him. When his actions do not constitute an innovation in religion, there is no objection to his keeping Israelite commandments, and they receive reward for it.
if he brought an olah, we accept it from him. And offer it. But we do not accept other offerings from him (Hilchot Ma'aseh HaKorbanot 3:2).

and it seems to me that we give it to the poor of Israel etc.. It is forbidden to accept charity from a gentile for the poor of Israel, and if he gives, it is distributed to gentile poor (Hilchot Matnot Aniyim 8:9). However, it is permitted to accept charity from the descendants of Noah, since when they are in need it is a mitzvah for Israelites to support them.
the gentile. An idol worshiper.
to judge them according to these laws. According to their commandments.
so that the world not be destroyed. When they have no system of justice and law.
by their laws. According to the rules of the laws of the descendants of Noah.

if there is a benefit to the Israelite in their laws etc.. For example, in damages caused by animals, where under their laws a person is not held liable for damage done by his animal (see Hilchot Nizkei Mamon 8:5).

as it says, 'to the stranger within your gates you shall give it, and he may eat it'. The Torah commands us to give a ger toshav animals that died of themselves, which are forbidden to us to eat (see also Hilchot Avodah Zarah 10:2).
even the gentiles, the Sages commanded... and to support their poor along with the poor of Israel, for the sake of peace. See also ibid. halachah 5, Hilchot Matnot Aniyim 7:7.
to its old state. To its original, former condition.
the first kingdom. At the time when the king from the House of David reigned over all Israel, before the kingdom was split into the kingdom of Judah and the kingdom of Israel (see I Kings 11:29-39).

and they will observe Shemitah and Jubilee years according to all their commandments stated in the Torah. For the commandments of Shemitah and Yovel apply by Torah law only when all Israel lives in the Land of Israel, not mixed tribe with tribe but each tribe on its own inheritance (see Hilchot Shemitah VeYovel 10:8-9). These commandments will return to apply by Torah law only after the King Messiah gathers all the dispersed of Israel and after each Israelite is traced by lineage and informed to which tribe he belongs (below, 12:3).

they include all the things that were said by the prophets. In the Torah the matters are stated in general terms, and the books of the Prophets expand and elaborate greatly on the subject of redemption.
also in the passage of Balaam it is stated. Balaam's blessings, too, mention the subject of redemption.
and there he prophesied about the two Messiahs. And not only about redemption in general.
about the first Messiah, who is David. Who was the first king anointed with a horn and whose kingship continued (see Babylonian Talmud Megillah 14a).
who saves Israel from the hand of the descendants of Esau. Redeems Israel from the final exile under the descendants of Esau, which is called the exile of Edom.
I see him, but not now. Not now, but at a later time.
I behold him, but not near. I will see him, but only in the distant future.
a star shall step forth from Jacob. A king will arise from the descendants of Jacob, for the king is raised above other people like a star.
a scepter. A ruler and governor.
and shall smite the corners of Moab. He will strike and break the rulers of Moab (see Targum Onkelos).

and he smote Moab and measured them with a line. And later there it says, 'and he measured two lines to put to death and one full line to keep alive,' which means that David measured Moab's soldiers with a rope and killed two-thirds of them.
and break down all the sons of Seth. He will rule over all people born from Seth, the son of Adam (see Targum Onkelos).
and his dominion shall be from sea to sea. The verse continues, 'and from the river to the ends of the earth,' meaning that he will rule over the whole world.
and Edom shall be a possession. Edom will be an inheritance for whoever conquers them.
and Seir shall be a possession of his enemies. He will inherit and rule over his enemies, who are descendants of Esau, called 'Seir'.
as it says, 'and saviors shall go up on Mount Zion'. The verse continues, 'to judge the mountain of Esau.'
also regarding the cities of refuge it says etc.. This is another proof of the future redemption from a commandment in the Torah.

and you shall add for yourself three more cities to these three. Israel was told that if their territory expands, they shall add three cities of refuge besides the cities of refuge they were commanded to set apart when they entered the Land of Israel.
and this never happened. That cities of refuge were added beyond the cities set apart in the days of Joshua son of Nun.

and the Holy One, blessed be He, did not command in vain. It cannot be that the Holy One, blessed be He, commanded the addition of these cities for nothing; rather it will surely come to pass in the future. These cities will be in the lands of the Kenites, Kenizzites and Kadmonites that were promised to our forefather Abraham and have not yet been conquered, and will be conquered in the days of the King Messiah (see Hilchot Rotzeach 8:4).

but with the words of the Prophets, the matter needs no proof etc.. It was necessary to detail the proofs from the Torah for the coming of the Messiah and the future redemption, but regarding the words of the Prophets there is no need, since they are full of descriptions of the redemption.
and similar to these things which fools say. Who think that the Messiah's purpose is to change the nature of the world.
Ben Kozeva the king. Known as Bar Kokhba, who led the revolt against the Romans.
and he and all the sages of his generation imagined that he was the King Messiah. See also Hilchot Ta'aniyot 5:3.
until he was killed for sins. The generation was not worthy of redemption, and Ben Kozeva was killed because of the sins of the generation.

and the main point of the matter is thus etc.. One of the fundamentals of religion is that there will be no change in the Torah and the commandments (see Hilchot Yesodei HaTorah 9:1, the introduction to Perek Chelek, ninth principle, and others). Therefore there is no doubt that whoever claims to be the Messiah and adds to or subtracts from the commandments, or interprets them as not literal, as the messiahs of Christianity and Islam did (see Hilchot Teshuvah 3:8 and below, halachah 4), is certainly a denier and is not the Messiah that the Torah meant.
and if a king arises from the House of David. A leader descended from King David arises.
who meditates on the Torah and occupies himself with the commandments like David his ancestor. He takes David's place in wisdom and fear of God and is fit to reign in his stead (see above, 1:7).

and compels all Israel to walk in it and to strengthen its breaches. He will engage in compelling all Israel to walk in the way of the Torah and in repairing the existing breaches in the observance of the commandments.
and fights the wars of the Lord etc.. See above, 4:10.
this is certainly the Messiah. He has fulfilled the mission of the King Messiah as described above, halachah 1.

and the Holy One, blessed be He, only set him up to test the many etc.. As part of a process of clarification and refinement that prepares the people for the end of days, when the Messiah promised by the Torah will be revealed.
and some of the wise shall stumble. Bar Kozeva, who was a great man and fit to be the Messiah, failed in his attempt to bring the redemption.

even Jesus of Nazareth etc.. Daniel prophesied not only about the righteous kings of Israel who were presumed to be the Messiah and failed, but also about false messiahs who would emerge from among the people of Israel.
and this Ishmaelite who arose after him. Muhammad, the founder of Islam.
are only to straighten the way for the King Messiah etc.. They are part of a process of preparing the world for the coming of the King Messiah, so that all will believe in the Lord and serve Him.

the world has already been filled with the words of the Messiah, the words of the Torah and the words of the commandments etc.. Through Christianity and Islam, the Torah has been spread and made known throughout the entire world.

these say that the commandments were true and have already been nullified in this time and did not apply for all generations. Some among the gentiles say that the Torah and the commandments did apply in the past, but in the present time they no longer apply.

and those say that there are hidden things in them and they are not as they appear, and the Messiah has already come and revealed their secrets. Others say that the commandments stated are not literal but hint at other hidden meanings revealed by the one whom they claim to be their Messiah.

and when the King Messiah truly arises etc.. Although today the gentiles who occupy themselves with the Torah distort its meaning, nevertheless when the King Messiah comes they will retract and understand that they erred. It turns out that the false messiahs who arose for the nations of the world caused them to occupy themselves with matters of the Torah and become aware of what is written in it, and thereby actually assisted the Messiah's work in the future.
that anything of the world's normal course will be nullified etc.. A change in the nature of creation will take place.

as it says, 'a wolf of the deserts shall plunder them, a leopard shall watch over their cities'. The verse compares the kingdoms of the nations to a wolf found in the wilderness that plunders, and to a leopard that hurries to attack their cities to ruin them.
and so everything similar to these things written about the Messiah. In the words of the Prophets.

but only the subjugation by the kingdoms. During the exile Israel is subjugated to the kingdoms of the nations, and in the days of the Messiah sovereignty will return to Israel (Hilchot Teshuvah 9:2).
the wars of Gog and Magog will be. See Ezekiel chapters 38-39.

to straighten Israel and prepare their hearts. To guide them to correct their deeds and prepare them to know God. He does not come to add or subtract anything in the Torah (Commentary on the Mishnah, Eduyot 8:7).
people who have a presumption of fitness. Who are presumed in the community to be fit to enter the congregation, and it is permitted to marry them.
but for the sake of peace in the world. To remove the baseless hatred that exists among people (ibid.).
and some of the Sages say that Elijah will come before the coming of the Messiah. And not at the beginning of his reign, as described in the previous paragraph.
even the Sages have no tradition about these matters. Our Sages have no tradition about these matters.
but only according to the weight of the verses. According to their interpretation of the verses.
the order of these events and their details are not a fundamental of the faith. The order of events and the exact manner in which they will occur are not among the foundations of belief.
let one not calculate the end times. Let him not make calculations to determine when the Messiah will come.
their minds are puffed up. It will blow away in the wind and vanish, for it has no substance.

rather, let him wait and believe in the matter as a whole, as we have explained. Let him wait and pray for the coming of the Messiah and believe in the fundamental matters concerning the definition and mission of the King Messiah, as explained above 11:1 (see Rambam's introduction to the chapter Chelek, the twelfth principle).
when his kingdom is established. When his kingship is firmly established.
all will be traced by his word. He will make known the true lineage of each person.
and he will sit as a refiner and purifier. He will sit in order to refine and purify Israel (based on Malachi 3:3).

and he will say: this one is of priestly lineage, etc.. In our time priests hold their status by presumption (chazakah), and do not have the status of priests of established lineage who may eat sacred foods and Torah-law terumah (see Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 20:1). Through the King Messiah they will have the status of priests of established lineage.

and he will reject those who are not of Israelite lineage. A person who was presumed to be a priest or Levite but is in fact not of the tribe of Levi, he will remove from his status and announce that he is an Israelite.

and the Tirshata said to them, etc.. Nehemiah (called "the Tirshata" - see Nehemiah 8:9) told the priests who could not prove their lineage not to eat terumah and sacred foods until a high priest would arise with Urim and Tummim who would reveal their lineage.
that a family that has been absorbed has been absorbed. A disqualified family that mixed into the community through lack of knowledge - its disqualification is not to be revealed.
as we explained in Hilchot Teshuvah. 9:2.

and the occupation of the whole world will be only to know the Lord. The King Messiah will be wiser than Solomon and will have a level of prophecy close to that of Moses our teacher; he will teach the people and instruct them in the way of God, and all the nations will come to hear him (Hilchot Teshuvah 9:2).
